identity_note: DART J1832-0911 and ASKAP J1832-0911 refer to the same long-period transient in the cited literature.

new_post_prereg_evidence.source: Li et al. 2026, Science Bulletin, DOI 10.1016/j.scib.2026.06.015
observations: DART period 2656.23 +/- 0.15 s, consistent with the ASKAP timing clock
plausible association with supernova remnant G22.7-0.2
dispersion measure, SNR CO emission, H I absorption and low chance-alignment probability are reported as mutually consistent with the association
phase-locked circular or nearly 100 percent linear polarization, interpreted as evidence for a strong geometrically stable magnetic field
no detectable optical counterpart even with a 10 m-class telescope
authors favor a young neutron-star origin whose spin may have been braked by fallback material
new_post_prereg_evidence.independence_value: New observing campaign and physical context beyond the 2025 ASKAP/X-ray discovery dataset.

new_post_prereg_evidence.source: Tsinghua University summary of the Science Bulletin result, 2026-07-01
observations: FAST detected a short approximately 0.2-second broadband pulse during a DART radio-quiet interval
the FAST pulse was reported as nearly 100 percent linearly polarized
new_post_prereg_evidence.boundary: Institutional summary of the peer-reviewed study; preserve as supporting description, not a substitute for the paper's quantitative tables.

new_post_prereg_evidence.source: Wang et al. 2025 Nature, DOI 10.1038/s41586-025-09077-w and supplementary discussion
observations: no secular or periodic TOA variations were detected in the published timing analysis and the period derivative was constrained
deep near-infrared non-detections disfavor ordinary luminous stellar companions

an eclipse-like X-ray dip was considered but a simple 44.2-minute compact-binary eclipse interpretation was described as geometrically problematic because the implied eclipse duration is too long for the allowed Roche-lobe scale
broadband highly polarized radio substructure is difficult to reconcile with simple accretion-stream radio emission

why_not_closed: The SNR association is described as plausible rather than a direct geometric distance lock.

The fallback-braking scenario explains how a young neutron star might reach an ultralong period, but the coherent radio and variable X-ray emission mechanism at that period remains physically challenging.
Alternative compact-object models are weakened, not mathematically eliminated.

impact_on_tesla_sweep: This is an exemplary demotion of apparent mystery. The 44-minute clock remains extraordinary, but accumulating localization, dispersion, polarization, SNR-context and multiwavelength evidence moves the source toward a natural compact-object interpretation instead of toward a message interpretation.
next_physical_questions: direct distance or astrometric test of the SNR association
phase stability of radio-Xray offset across multiple epochs
polarization geometry and mode changes across the 44-minute cycle
fallback-disc braking predictions versus period derivative and age
mechanism capable of producing broadband coherent substructure below second scales at an ultralong spin period
